newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia must sign De Beers deal -deputy min.
newsitem.headline: Russia must sign De Beers deal -deputy min.

text.p: Russia must sign a trade agreement with South African diamond group De Beers, First Deputy Economy Minister Vladimir Panskov was quoted as saying on Thursday.

"If this agreement is not signed, we will simply destroy the world diamond market. Neither the De Beers company nor Russia will be able to work normally without such an agreement," Interfax quoted Panskov as saying.
The finance ministry earlier on Thursday issued a statement saying Russia was ready to cooperate with De Beers.
De Beers on Wednesday gave the Russian government until the end of 1996 to approve a diamond trade agreement and said it would otherwise terminate an interim arrangement.

De Beers controls about three quarters of the world diamond market and Russia accounts for about 25 percent of all rough gems De Beers sells. A five-year deal expired in December 1995 and was replaced by a memorandum signed in February 1996.

Panskov said that before Russia and De Beers signed the memorandum "we studied this problem for a long time and came to the conclusion that an agreement is advantageous and necessary for Russia both from the point of view of output of rough diamonds and of sales of gems on the world market".
Panskov said that in the course of work on the agreement. differences of opinion between Russian diamond producer Almazy Rossii-Sakha, domestic gem processing plants and De Beers had become clear.
"But I think that in any circumstances we cannot set off on the road of mutual ultimatums."
